ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is the curve of y=f(x), and the four x values a, b, c, d are marked. On the left side, near a, the curve decreases to the right; near b, the curve increases to the right; near c, the curve decreases to the right and becomes steeper and steeper; on the right branch, near d, the curve decreases to the right, but gradually becomes flatter. Then reason: f'(x) negative means the tangent slope is negative, that is, the function is decreasing; f'(x) increasing means the slope value is increasing, that is, the negative slope becomes not so negative. At b the slope is positive, so it does not conform. At a and c, although the slope is negative, looking to the right the slope becomes more negative, so f' is decreasing. At d the curve decreases but gradually becomes flatter, and the slope is negative and is increasing. Therefore the one that conforms to the conditions is d.

raw_record.question_text: The graph of y = f(x) is shown above. At which labeled value of x is f'(x) negative and increasing?

method.method_draft: Inspect the graph at each labeled x-value and use local tangent behavior. From the image, the curve at b is rising, so f'(b) is positive. At a and c the curve is falling, so f' is negative there, but the nearby slopes become more steeply negative as x moves right, so f' is decreasing rather than increasing. At d, on the right-hand branch, the curve is falling but flattening out as x increases; its tangent slope is negative but becoming less negative. Therefore f'(x) is negative and increasing at d.

method.method_draft: Translate the condition into monotonicity plus concavity: f'(x)<0 means f is decreasing, and f'(x) increasing means f''(x)>0, so the graph of f should be decreasing and concave up at the labeled point. The point d is on a decreasing branch that bends upward, so it is decreasing and concave up. Hence the labeled value is d.
